body:
## Summary

Implements support for external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor) in hive-agent, enabling wasp.sh compatibility.

## Changes

- New CodingAgentProvider (packages/hive-agent/lib/coding-agent.js):
  - Detects available coding agents on the system (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor)
  - Delegates inference tasks to the detected agent via CLI
  - Falls back to local providers (MockProvider/QvacProvider) for non-coding tasks
  - Cross-runtime compatible (works on both Bare and Node.js using bare-env)
  - Configurable timeout, working directory, and fallback provider

- Added coding capability to CAPABILITIES in packages/hive-agent/lib/provider.js

- Updated providerFromPersona factory in packages/hive-agent/index.js:
  - Supports runtime: "coding-agent" in persona config
  - Supports fallback: "mock" or fallback: "qvac" for non-coding tasks
  - Supports agent field to specify preferred coding agent

- Tests in test/agent.js:
  - Tests coding agent detection
  - Tests capabilities advertising
  - Tests provider factory selection

## Usage

A persona can now use external coding agents:

{
  "runtime": "coding-agent",
  "agent": "claude-code",
  "system_prompt": "You are a coding assistant",
  "fallback": "mock"
}

This matches the wasp.sh / Buzz workflow where agents detect available coding harnesses on the system and use them.

## Testing

All 190 tests pass (3 new tests added for the coding agent provider).

comments.body:
@qwadratic Deeper agent functionality **is** planned — driving real coding agents from relay mentions is the direction, not a detour. So this is about the shape of the first version, not the idea.

Concerns, in order:

**1. No sender gating.** `agent.js:223` subscribes on `#p: [this.pubkey]`, so any pubkey that mentions the agent reaches `turn()` → `provider.complete()`. On an open relay that is a stranger's message becoming `claude -p "<their text>" --max-turns 10`. No `allowlist`/`allowedPubkeys` exists in `packages/hive-agent`.

**2. No tool restrictions.** `#getAgentArgs` emits `[-p, prompt, --max-turns, 10]` — no `--allowedTools`, no `--permission-mode`, no sandbox. Combined with (1) that is remote code execution by DM.

**3. `workDir` defaults to the relay's own cwd.** `opts.workDir ?? getCwd()`, and nothing passes `workDir`. The agent runs in the checkout it is serving from.

**4. `env: { ...getEnv() }`** hands over the full operator environment, API keys included.

Two things that are not security but block the merge regardless:

**5. It cannot fire today.** `agent.js:10` still does `require("./qvac")`, and this PR does not touch `agent.js`. A `runtime: "coding-agent"` persona falls through `qvac.js:159-178` and gets a MockProvider. The combined factory in `index.js` is only reachable from the tests.

**6. The test asserts detection fails** — `t.exception(provider.ready(), /No coding agent found/)`. It passes on CI because CI has no `claude` installed; on a laptop that has it, it fails. A test that only passes when the feature is absent is not testing the feature.

Suggested shape for v1: required `allowedRequesters` (absent = refuse, never allow-all), required isolated `workDir`, allowlisted env, read-only flag sets per agent — and any agent without a known read-only mode dropped from `CODING_AGENTS` rather than defaulted. Plus the test that matters: a mention from a non-allowed pubkey asserting `spawn` was called **zero** times.

Marking as draft rather than closing, since the goal is one we want.

title: feat(hive-agent): add CodingAgentProvider for external coding agent support (wasp.sh compatibility)
